filing_guidance.title: Delhi High Court filing preparation
filing_guidance.scope: High Court of Delhi e-filing preparation only. Case type, filing stage, jurisdiction and current registry directions still require advocate review.

requirements.title: High Court e-file size
requirements.detail: Maximum 300 MB. Above 300 MB, the notification directs the advocate or litigant to a Designated Centre for intranet e-filing.

requirements.title: Draft document format
requirements.detail: A4; Times New Roman 14; 1.5 line spacing; quotations and indents at 12 with single spacing; 4 cm left and right margins; 2 cm top and bottom.

requirements.title: Searchability and bookmarks
requirements.detail: The court-hosted FAQ says bookmarking is compulsory and recommends 300 DPI scanning with OCR. OCR output still requires visual and legal review.
requirements.source_label: Delhi High Court Online e-Filing FAQ

requirements.title: Party details
requirements.detail: The court-hosted FAQ says details of every petitioner and respondent are mandatory in the fresh-case workflow.
requirements.source_label: Delhi High Court Online e-Filing FAQ, Q18-Q19

requirements.title: 2026 online upload implementation notice
requirements.detail: The IT Cell notice dated 6 February 2026 implements the 300 MB online e-file limit from 11:00 a.m. on 7 February 2026. The High Court notification separately provides a Designated Centre route for larger e-files. District-court limits are a different scope.
requirements.source_label: Delhi High Court IT Cell · 6 February 2026

templates.title: Memo of Parties upload template
templates.purpose: Court-provided spreadsheet for party data used by the e-filing facility.

templates.title: Urgent listing / accommodation form
templates.purpose: Official form for urgent mentioning cases; applicability and current process must be confirmed.

templates.title: Interlocutory applications form
templates.purpose: Official interlocutory-application form published on the Forms & Proformas page.

source_conflicts: 17 November 2026: the Rule 3.4 amendment and IT Cell implementation notice were rechecked. Other inherited references retain their earlier review date; no advocate approval has been obtained.
The older FAQ states a 50 MB online limit. The later 2026 amendment substitutes Rule 3.4 and sets the High Court maximum e-file size at 300 MB.

The common-objections page contains older paper-format references, including foolscap. Do not use those references to override the later A4 Practice Directions without advocate and registry confirmation.
Common objections help prevent defects but are not a complete required-document checklist for every case type or filing stage.

name: Court-neutral preparation (technical only)
description: Configurable PDF preparation without built-in court requirements or a filing-compliance claim. Confirm the destination court, case type and stage separately.

name: Supreme Court of India (source-linked draft)
description: Source-linked preparation reference only. No advocate approval or case-specific completeness determination. No automatic portal-size cap is applied.

filing_guidance.title: Supreme Court of India filing reference
filing_guidance.scope: Supreme Court e-filing portal reference. Petition type, stage, applicable rules and amendments need separate review; this is not a filing-completeness checklist.

requirements.title: Petition upload format and size
requirements.detail: The SC-eFM 3.0 FAQ, question 12, describes PDF uploads with a 50 MB maximum and splitting larger files. Confirm the portal used; this is not a cap on the entire ZIP package. No automatic limit is applied by this draft profile.

requirements.title: Petition forms and procedural requirements
requirements.detail: Question 14 directs users to the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 for petition templates. The applicable proceeding and later amendments must be identified before a required-document checklist can be evaluated.

requirements.title: Choose the actual filing service
requirements.detail: The official e-filing page links both SC-eFM 2.0 and SC-eFM 3.0. Confirm the route before relying on portal guidance.

source_conflicts: No advocate has approved this profile. Source research is not legal sign-off.
The 50 MB FAQ statement is upload guidance; MatterDraft’s general all-artifact size cap has different semantics and is deliberately not set automatically.
The January 2025 scrutiny-checklist PDF could not be retrieved during this pass; its detailed requirements are not encoded.

name: Punjab and Haryana High Court (source-linked draft)
description: Source-linked preparation reference only. No advocate approval or case-specific completeness determination. No automatic portal-size cap is applied.

filing_guidance.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court filing reference
filing_guidance.scope: High Court of Punjab and Haryana, Chandigarh: reference to official filing resources. Civil, criminal and writ proceedings have distinct objection checklists; no single required-document list is inferred.

requirements.title: Check current software and notices
requirements.detail: The official notice index lists a new e-filing software notice effective 25 September 2026, alongside earlier 2026 and 2025 guidance. The notice body could not be retrieved here; confirm its instructions before relying on an older workflow.

requirements.title: Use the checklist for the proceeding
requirements.detail: The official website provides separate Civil, Criminal and Writ objection-checklist links. Their current detailed contents were not retrieved in this pass. Select the applicable proceeding and review the original checklist.

requirements.title: Filing portal and assistance
requirements.detail: Use the court’s own e-filing page to reach its portal, manuals and assistance resources. This application prepares documents locally and does not submit them to the court.

source_conflicts: No advocate has approved this profile. Current case-specific and conditional requirements remain unverified.
The January 2025 guideline has time-limited and category-specific provisions. It must not be treated as a current universal filing mandate.
No verified current upload-size cap was obtained. The draft leaves the technical cap unset rather than borrowing another court’s limit.
